final_answer: Merge sort is a divide-and-conquer algorithm. It splits the list into halves recursively until each sublist has one element. Then, it merges the sublists back together in sorted order. Merging compares the front elements of each sublist and appends the smaller one to the result. This continues until all elements are merged. Merge sort has O(n log n) time complexity in all cases. For linked lists, it is preferred over quicksort because quicksort relies on random access and partitioning, which is inefficient for linked lists. Merge sort can split and merge linked lists with minimal overhead, and its stable sorting behavior helps maintain order when duplicates exist.
